title: The broken request
summary: Validate an HTTP response and parse JSON without trusting the wire.

scenario.briefing: The storefront calls the orders API. A proxy returned an HTML error page and a 500, but the client still tried to read an order. Repair parseOrderResponse so status and body are checked before use.

objectives.description: Distinguish successful and failed HTTP statuses.
Reject malformed or incomplete response bodies.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Response status 200 or 201 means success for this endpoint.
JSON.parse throws on malformed text. The caller still needs a structured failure result.
A valid body must contain an id string.
Return {ok:true, orderId:id} for 200/201 with a valid id, otherwise {ok:false, error:...} with invalid-json, invalid-body, or server-error.

misconceptions.description: Treating a 500 response body as a valid order.
misconceptions.feedback: HTTP status is part of the response contract. A server error may have a body, but it is not a successful order.

misconceptions.description: Letting JSON.parse failure escape as an unhandled exception.
misconceptions.testDescription: Malformed JSON is reported, not thrown.
misconceptions.feedback: Malformed JSON is an expected boundary condition. Catch it and return a structured error the caller can handle.

misconceptions.description: Treating a JSON body as proof that the request succeeded.
misconceptions.feedback: Status and body carry different information. A 500 response can contain valid JSON that describes the failure.

misconceptions.description: Believing valid JSON always means the request succeeded.
misconceptions.feedback: Parsing proves only that the text is JSON. The status and the body's fields must still be checked.

sections.title: HTTP is a contract
sections.body: A response has a status code and headers and a body. 2xx means the request succeeded, 4xx means the client request was unacceptable, and 5xx means the server failed. The body still needs validation because a proxy or bug can return unexpected content.

sections.title: Parse at the boundary
sections.body: Network data is untrusted text until parsed and checked. JSON.parse can fail. A parsed object can be missing required fields. Boundary validation turns unpredictable input into a small, typed result the rest of the program can handle.

vocabulary.definition: A three-digit number summarizing the response outcome.
A text format for structured data.

steps.title: Read the status

options.label: Yes, because the body is JSON
No, 500 means the server failed; report the failure

quiz.explanation: The 5xx status signals a server-side failure. A JSON body can describe the failure, but it is not a successful order.

hints: Decide whether a 500 response can still be a successful order.
The status code summarizes the outcome; a JSON error body is still an error.
A delivery notice with a tracking number is not a delivered parcel if the carrier marked it failed.
500 means server failure, so report it even though the body parses as JSON.
Implement parseOrderResponse so success and each failure case return the documented shape.
Check the status first, then parse safely, then validate the body.
For 400 with {"error":"invalid"}, return {ok:false,error:"invalid"}; for unparseable text, return invalid-json.
Branch on 2xx, wrap JSON.parse in try and catch, require an id for success, and return stable error codes.
